units.text: Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13. And according to Mark Gurman, it sounds like the rumored MacBook Pro redesign will arrive shortly after.
Redesigned MacBook Pro with touchscreen to be introduced in October or November, per Mark Gurman

Today Bloomberg launched a new weekly podcast: ‘Power On with Mark Gurman.’ In the inaugural episode, Gurman provides a launch timing update for Apple’s rumored new MacBook Pro redesign with a touchscreen, OLED, and more.
Here’s what he said:

Apple, I believe, will introduce its first touchscreen MacBook Pro this fall, as early as October. It could slip to November, but as early as October. And Apple is testing it internally using macOS 27.2, which is a beta that they’ve already put out to developers in recent weeks. So this thing is approaching.
Apple often launches new Macs in the late October-early November window. It sounds like that’s exactly what’s being planned for this new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) device.

We’ve long been expecting and hoping for a fall launch, but Gurman previously cautioned that the product could slip into early 2027. Now that October has arrived, today’s new update is a great indication that the model is on track to launch soon.
And based on Gurman’s other reporting, it sounds like we could see several new Apple products launch within a few weeks of each other.

A new Apple TV 4K, ‘HomePad’, and HomePod mini are rumored for October 13, with Macs following in late October or early November. And that’s all in addition to the highly anticipated iPhone Duo, which ships October 23.

units.text: Apple has added another raft of movies to watch for free with an Apple TV subscription, while seemingly not yet removing all of the previous set.

Apple has famously not bought any broadcaster or streamer's library of titles, but from early on it has bought the occasional film. Now following one tranche of titles back in August, Apple TV has added still more, all included in its subscription.

Unless you buy out an entire library, then for historical reasons of how films are distributed worldwide, it is extraordinarily complex to acquire the rights to individual titles. Apple has not secured global rights to all of its new titles, either, meaning that different films are available in different countries.
In the US, Apple has now added:
28 Days Later
American Gangster
Black Hawk Down
Blood Diamond
Fallen
Fury
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
Going the Distance
Good Will Hunting
Insomnia
Jurassic World
Taxi Driver
Tropic Thunder
In the UK, for example, the newly added titles are:
Godzilla
Inception
Jurassic World
The Martian
The Social Network
Spider-Man: Far from Home
The Town
War of the Worlds (2005 version)
That's a significant expansion for the UK, which in August only saw 6 movies added to the US's 19.

While at least most of August's additions appear to still be available in the US, don't expect any of them to last. They will have been acquired for a specific period only, and Apple has not said what that period is.
Given how the UK, at least, has already lost some titles, if there is a film you want to see, you should watch it now.

Note that this only applies to these newly added classic movies. For everything that Apple TV has made itself, or acquired such as the Oscar-winning "CODA," you can reasonably expect films to stay for years.

Then lately Apple TV has been getting most attention and awards for its television dramas and comedies. But it is still producing films, such as the next movie from "CODA" writer/director Sian Heder, "Being Heumann."

units.text: Apple's forthcoming Home Hub is already expected to tailor its display and data to different users, but now it appears it will do so using AI facial recognition instead of Face ID.

The long-expected Home Hub, or HomePod with a screen, is now expected to be launched on October 13, 2026, and more details including colors are continuing to leak out in advance. Now in Bloomberg's new "Power On" podcast, it's claimed that the device will use AI facial recognition.

It's been expected since the very first rumors of the device that it would present different content for different users in a household. So depending on which family member is using the device, they would automatically get their photos, music, calendar events, and so on.

That's likely to be done in part by the device looking for iPhones in the proximity, but it's also been presumed that it would use Face ID to identify the current user. Now according to Bloomberg, there will be exactly this user-switching and there will be facial recognition, but not Face ID.
Why Apple might not use Face ID

The AI facial recognition technology to be used is described only as being highly technical, and there is no explanation for why it isn't Face ID. Extrapolating from other Apple Home system leaks, it's possible that this is the same technology that will be used in future security cameras.

Rather than either scanning a face when someone stands in front of the sensor, such a system could continuously monitor its environment. In the case of the security camera system, it could do this and only trigger recordings when activity is spotted.
So perhaps the Home Hub will constantly monitor its surroundings but only actively identify a user when that person interacts with it from anywhere in the room.

The same report also repeats earlier claims that Apple has had this device manufactured and ready to ship for a considerable time. It's believed that its launch was held back while Apple waited for the improved Siri AI to be released.

Also about to be released is the updated MacBook Pro, currently expected in October or November. This same podcast report also repeats an earlier expectation that this MacBook Pro will be the first to feature a Dynamic Island.

units.text: As reported by 404 Media, Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass the iPhone security feature that automatically reboots devices if they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours. Here are the details.
A bit of context
Nearly two years ago, the iOS 18.1 update introduced Inactivity Reboot, a feature that forces iPhone reboots in case they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours.

In essence, this feature makes it harder for law enforcement and forensic tools to access data on a locked iPhone, since a reboot causes the device to return to a Before First Unlock (BFU) state, rather than remaining in the less restrictive After First Unlock (AFU) state.

When an iPhone is in BFU, certain sensitive data remains protected by encryption keys that only become available after the user enters their passcode for the first time, thus putting the device in AFU.
From that point on, more of the device’s data remains accessible until the iPhone is rebooted again, which returns it to BFU.

Automatically rebooting an iPhone means that even if a device is seized by law enforcement, it can return to BFU before investigators can access it, since obtaining a warrant or transporting the device to a forensic lab can take time.
As 404 Media noted when iOS 18.1 was released, the feature can also make it harder for thieves or other bad actors to keep a stolen iPhone in AFU long enough to develop or use a way to break into it.
GrayKey reportedly gets around Inactivity Reboot

404 Media reported today that, based on an “educational and tutorial video, which was made exclusively for law enforcement agents and appears to be dated early 2025,” Magnet Forensics, the company behind the GrayKey phone unlocking tool, appears to have developed a way to bypass the iPhone’s Inactivity Reboot feature.
According to the report, Magnet developed a new device called GrayKey Preserve, as well as an Evidence Preservation Mode for its existing GrayKey hardware.

Both are reportedly designed to maintain an iPhone’s forensic state without immediately exposing the data stored on the device, allowing law enforcement to keep that state intact while waiting for authorization to search it.
The report notes that while the video doesn’t detail the technical mechanism behind the workaround, it explains that GrayKey can preserve an iPhone’s AFU state even if the device reboots.
From the report:

“That AFU state is captured,” by GrayKey Preserve and Evidence Preservation Mode, the employee says. “Even if that device does reboot for any number of reasons, memory maintenance or the power is lost or whatever, the AFU state is not lost. This is the true magic behind the GrayKey Preserve and the Evidence Preservation Mode function.”

404 Media reached out to Apple and Magnet Forensics, but neither responded to a request for comment. They also consulted iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen, who said Magnet may have found a way to manipulate the iPhone’s clock, or to turn off the processes responsible for expiring certain data altogether.

While the video appears to date from early 2025, it is unclear how long the technology has been available to law enforcement, whether it has been used in actual investigations, or whether the workaround remains effective against the latest versions of iOS.

units.text: 苹果全球零售门店正在为新一轮产品展示更新进行准备。多家苹果零售店本周收到了一批贴有“Do Not Open Until October 8（10月8日前禁止开启）”标签的保密箱体，引发外界对苹果即将发布新产品的猜测。
据了解，这些箱体被认为装有新的零售展示材料，包括产品标签、宣传图像以及门店陈列布局所需的相关物料，供苹果员工在新产品发布前后更新店内展示区域。相关消息最初来自知情人士爆料，随后获得进一步确认。
目前尚不清楚这些保密物料对应的具体产品。有分析认为，其内容可能与苹果即将推出的折叠屏手机iPhone Duo有关。不过，从保密等级以及时间安排来看，更大的可能是与苹果即将进军智能家居领域的新硬件产品有关。

units.text: Sporting a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score, the extreme mountain climbing documentary “The Last First: Winter K2” is now available to Apple TV subscribers. Watch the trailer below.
’A complex, harrowing and moving story’
A few weeks ago, Apple TV released the trailer for “The Last First: Winter K2” and celebrated reaching a 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes’ Tomatometer.
The documentary, which has also premiered in selected theaters in recent days, promises “an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture.”

“The Last First: Winter K2” is directed by Amir Bar-Lev (The Tillman Story, Long Strange Trip – The Untold Story of The Grateful Dead) and focuses on a 2021 expedition to the summit of Mount Godwin-Austen, better known as K2.
Here’s Apple TV on what subscribers can expect from “The Last First: Winter K2”:

Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life-and-death circumstances.

units.text: Apple’s rumored push into smart home tech could include a smart home security camera that only gives users text event descriptions instead of video footage. Mark Gurman said in the first episode of the Power On podcast that the camera will be part of “a new Apple smart home ecosystem,” alongside Apple’s rumored smart home hub:

> They’re also building home security products, both first-party and third-party home security products. And the biggest thing is a program called J450. And this is an offshoot and a companion product to the J490 smart home display. And these are little cameras that you can put around your house. They have very low frame rate. It looks like a cylinder. It looks like a metal giant, you know, chapstick.
> And what does that mean? No video recording. So it’s a sensor that cannot actually pull in real video footage. It’s analyzing your environment in your home and around your home simply using AI.
Gurman also mentions that the camera uses “a very similar technology” to what Apple’s reportedly developing for a pair of AirPods with cameras that leaked earlier this year.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ms-uSU7-1Hs]

Instead of using something like mmWave for presence sensing, using an image sensor with AI embedded that processes everything on-device, like these Sony IMX500 sensors, could work without passing images that would need to be stored and secured. Apple Home currently has a “Detect Activity” setting for HomeKit Secure Video cameras that stops video streaming and recording, but continues tracking motion, similar to what Gurman describes.

He goes on to add that the smart home camera will have facial recognition for things like detecting when someone enters a room, but, “You’re not getting anything but text descriptions. There’s nothing you can do with it. There’s no video recording.”

units.text: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo on September 9 at the company's "Surprise and Shine" event. Apple's first foldable is the biggest shake-up of the iPhone design in almost a decade, and it's sure to be one of the hardest devices in years to actually get your hands on. If you're keen to be among the first owners of an iPhone Duo, here are some tips on how to give yourself the best chance.

Apple says preorders for the iPhone Duo will go live on at 5:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23 in more than 70 countries and regions, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, India, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Türkiye, the UAE, the UK, the U.S., and Vietnam. iPhone Duo will be available in 28 other countries and regions beginning Friday, October 30.
Initial stocks are expected to be extremely limited. Here are several tips that will greatly increase your chances of getting hold of one on launch day.

Get Ready for your iPhone Duo pre-order: Apple says you will be able to access its "Get Ready" feature through its online store and in the Apple Store app on October 12, one day before pre-orders go live. Make sure you do: it allows you to prepare your purchase by selecting your preferred model, confirming carrier status, adding accessories, choosing an AppleCare+ plan, and setting up payment methods. Afterwards, when pre-orders begin, you'll be able to complete your purchase with just a tap.

Check your Apple Account details beforehand: Do the necessary checks that confirm your payment method hasn't expired, your billing address matches your card, and your shipping address is the place you actually want the foldable iPhone sent to.

Get your trade-in quote in advance: Getting a trade-in valuation on your current iPhone adds more screens to the checkout process, so get it done before pre-orders go live. After a trade-in estimate is generated, Apple has to receive your old device within 14 days (15 days in Canada) to ensure you get the estimated value. But this countdown only comes into effect after you receive the iPhone Duo – not before.

If you financed your current phone through the old iPhone Upgrade Program, check your status and your replacement financing options now: Apple discontinued the old program in the US in July 2026. Eligible existing members can move to Apple Upgrade, Apple Card Monthly Installments, carrier financing, or a one-time purchase. Note that in the UK, Apple is in the process of transitioning former Upgrade Program customers to its Flexible Finance Account.

Open the Apple Store app ahead of time: Ensure you have the app up-to-date, open, and with your saved configuration on screen several minutes before pre-orders go live. The store does not always become accessible to every customer at exactly the advertised second. In fact, it's more likely to open up a few minutes later than that. Also: keep Apple's online store open in a browser on another device. Going on previous pre-orders, which of the two comes back first can vary by launch.

Don't change your configuration selection at checkout: Every change you make to your basket likely re-queries Apple's inventory. If your saved specification is available, take it all the way to payment. This includes which color you prefer – the more last-minute changes you make, the greater the risk becomes that availability will change before you check out.

Choose in-store pickup if it's offered: There's every reason to believe that Apple's pickup inventory will be allocated separately from its delivery stock, so a store slot can still be available after delivery estimates have slipped. Opting for in-store pickup also removes any potential ambiguity surrounding your estimated delivery window.

Launch day walk-in stock is a genuine alternative: Apple could conceivably hold back some inventory for in-store purchases on launch morning. Brick-and-mortar stocks are also allocated per store rather than nationally. Apple's pickup availability checker updates through the morning and is likely to be more efficient and reliable than calling the store. That being said, don't assume you'll be able to walk into a store and pick up an iPhone Ultra.
For all further details on features and specifications for the iPhone Duo, be sure to check out our dedicated roundup.

units.text: It's easier to crack an iPhone after it's been unlocked once by the user after a reboot. A law enforcement tool vendor may have found a way to keep the device in that state.

Magnet Forensics claims its tools preserve iPhone data that Apple's security features would otherwise make harder to access. The tools could give police more time to extract sensitive information from seized devices.
In iOS 18.1, Apple introduced a new privacy feature, a sort of inactivity reboot. This reboot restarts an iPhone after 72 hours without an unlock, returning it to a Before First Unlock (BFU) state.
That state restricts access to encryption keys. As a result, it makes it much harder for anyone to break into an iPhone using brute-force or other methods.

Now, a law enforcement educational video seen by 404 Media details a device called GrayKey Preserve. Magnet also offers Evidence Preservation Mode for its existing GrayKey hardware, which police use to access locked smartphones.

In the video, which was dated early 2025, Magnet says GrayKey Preserve keeps the device in the more accessible After First Unlock (AFU) state, even if an iPhone reboots. Evidence Preservation Mode also reportedly prevents cached locations, recently deleted photos, and iMessages from expiring, preserving them indefinitely.

After initial access, GrayKey Preserve disables cellular, Bluetooth, and Wi-Fi connections to isolate the phone from incoming communications. Evidence Preservation Mode then allows law enforcement to effectively freeze the data while waiting for authorization to attempt retrieval.
The video doesn't explain how the feature works. But, iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen believes it could be clock manipulation. It could also disable iPhone tasks that set data to expire.

units.text: 苹果正在开发一款面向全家的智能家居中枢，可用于与Siri AI互动、控制HomeKit设备、观看视频、查看日历和天气等信息。现有消息称，这款设备预计于10月13日与新款Apple TV 4K和HomePod mini一同亮相，售价可能在350美元左右，但设计、售价和上市安排都尚未得到苹果确认。
据传家居中枢将提供两种版本，均配备约6英寸、接近正方形的触摸屏，边框约四分之一英寸宽，尺寸大致相当于两台iPhone并排，厚度则接近iPhone。一款可挂墙安装，另一款配有半球形扬声器底座，外形类似iMac G4，屏幕通过抛光金属支臂连接，并可前后倾斜。壁挂版底部较薄，可贴合墙面，内置扬声器和麦克风。
两款据称都会采用灰色铝制外观，正面配备1080p摄像头，可用于FaceTime通话、用户认证和识别家庭成员；设备没有内置电池，需要通过USB-C连接电源。
设备可感知用户与屏幕的距离，并根据情境调整界面，例如无人靠近时显示室温，有人走近时切换到恒温器控制画面。相关传感器也可能用于智能家居自动化，例如有人进入房间时自动开灯，并据称可识别不同家庭成员及手势，实现更远距离的操控。
用户识别预计结合类似Face ID的功能与语音认证，设备可切换至当前使用者的个人资料和界面。由于摄像头识别准确度可能不及Face ID，语音可作为替代方式；用户还可通过iPhone设置二次认证。访客模式则会隐藏个人信息。另有传闻称，屏幕边缘设有类似Mac指示灯的环形灯光，可在暗处辅助设备识别用户。
家居中枢预计搭载A18或更新芯片，以支持Apple Intelligence，内存至少为8GB。内部系统代号据称为“Charismatic”，上市时也可能改称homeOS；系统将融合tvOS、watchOS和iOS的部分元素，并与iPhone同步，简化设备设置流程。

设备不会配备专属App Store，但预计预装多款苹果应用，包括Safari、Apple News、Apple Music、Apple Podcasts、备忘录、日历、照片、家庭、信息、提醒事项和FaceTime。主界面可自定义，并通过小组件显示天气、家庭控制、照片幻灯片和日程等内容；内置摄像头可识别不同家庭成员，为每个人呈现不同应用和主屏幕。界面被描述为结合watchOS与iPhone待机显示模式，闲置时重点展示时钟和照片幻灯片，也提供软件底座、应用启动器、可重新排列的图标以及类似Apple Watch的图标设计。用户还可浏览小组件图库、使用智能叠放，让小组件随时间轮换；连接的iPhone带来的小组件，只有主要用户在家时才会显示内容。整体视觉风格将围绕Siri AI打造，并采用较深色的设计元素。
该设备可加入HomeKit场景，支持播放视频，用户可以在厨房观看食谱步骤；家中部署多台设备时，还可作为房间间的对讲系统。内置扬声器支持音乐播放，并能作为AirPlay接收器。苹果另在开发一款可连接家居中枢的室内安防摄像头，预计2027年推出，传闻强调隐私保护，目标是提供Ring和Nest等产品之外的选择。

此外，该产品有可能不支持 App Store，但能够支持日历、天气、音乐、信息、提醒事项等程序。设备能够识别不同家庭用户，并根据用户不同，显示个性化小组件。

units.text: AppleCare coverage for the iPhone Duo will mean inexpensive repairs for Apple's first foldable, including $99 full inner display replacement or $19 "cover layer" swaps.
Apple's iPhone Duo may be the most complex and expensive iPhone to date, but thankfully it appears to be inexpensive to repair. At least, that will be the case if you have AppleCare.

According to Apple's service and repair website, first discovered by Quinn Nelson of SnazzyLabs, the iPhone Duo has a swappable cover layer that will cost just $19 with active AppleCare coverage. Of course, this will mean going to an Authorized Apple Service Provider to get it done.
Other AppleCare repair costs include $29 for front display or back glass repairs and a $99 inner display repair. Accidental damage repair is also $99 and theft or loss replacement is $149.

An interview with Apple's VP of hardware engineering Kate Bergeron, shared by 9to5Mac, reveals that Apple's intention with the removable cover layer is an option for user replacement after wearing in the existing layer. She said that Apple engineered the cover layer to wear in for as long as possible before a user might need to replace it.
Don't try this at home, for now

Since we're talking AppleCare, that means that the layer likely isn't meant to be "user" replaceable, though we won't know how easy it is to get off or put a new one back on until testing can be done. There is a small chance that Apple's self-service website will provide users a path to purchasing their own display cover layer.
AppleCare coverage for iPhone Duo will be much cheaper than paying for repairs without it

If it is easily peeled off, there is also an opportunity for third-party alternative outer layers. I could imagine different textures for Apple Pencil, privacy layers, or glossy covers that are more durable overall.

Obviously, Apple has engineered iPhone Duo and its hinge mechanism to account for the exact thickness and material of its first-party cover layer. Knowing Apple, this isn't some kind of simple screen protector-like surface and isn't intended for novice user replacement or third-party alternatives.
Going without one likely isn't an option either.

Whatever the case, wait to let the YouTubers with too much time and money to break a few iPhone Duos before trying any of this yourself. Chances are that any alternative cover layer could potentially damage the iPhone Duo and even invalidate the warranty and AppleCare.
iPhone Duo goes up for pre-order on October 16 and ships on October 23. It starts at $1,999 with 256GB of storage.

units.text: 苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo发布后，不仅在开发者社区引发热烈讨论，也让不少曾参与微软Surface Duo项目的现任和前任员工感慨万千。随着越来越多开发者展示围绕新形态打造的应用体验，一场关于“微软是否过早放弃Surface Duo”的讨论再次升温。
微软前技术顾问马特·维洛索曾担任微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉的技术顾问长达四年。他在社交平台上戏称，看到苹果发布iPhone Duo后，“某个地方有上千名参与Surface Duo项目的人正把脸埋进枕头里尖叫”。这番言论迅速引发共鸣。
Surface Duo于2020年正式推出，而苹果的iPhone Duo则在六年后登场。与此同时，微软在2023年取消了后续产品计划，因此不少业内人士认为，苹果如今展示的产品形态与理念，正是微软当年试图探索却未能成功延续的方向。
在iPhone Duo发布后的近三周时间里，社交媒体上持续出现围绕该设备的热门讨论。大量开发者已经开始为新形态设计创新应用，即便产品尚未正式发售。相比之下，开发者生态一直是Surface Duo面临的最大挑战之一。由于软件支持不足，加之系统优化问题，微软始终未能充分发挥双屏设备的潜力。
不少观察人士指出，微软实际上拥有数年的先发优势。当年公司不仅拥有相关硬件、软件平台和开发工具，还投入了大量研究资源。然而由于市场表现不佳以及生态建设进展缓慢，这一产品线最终被终止。
更让部分前微软员工感到复杂的是，苹果此次宣传iPhone Duo时采用的许多展示方式，与Surface Duo在2020年的宣传理念高度相似。无论是将设备当成迷你笔记本使用、支持多任务并行操作、通过不同折叠姿态完成工作，还是手写笔配合生产力应用的展示，都让许多熟悉Surface Duo的人产生强烈既视感。
微软副总裁斯科特·汉塞尔曼对此简短回应称：“安息吧，Surface Duo。永远只是伴娘。”这番评价被许多用户视为对产品命运的概括。微软能源业务首席技术官刘易斯·理查兹则用调侃方式回应称，他把苹果发布视频分享给朋友后，对方开玩笑说：“再过一周，苹果可能连‘Duo’这个词都是自己发明的了。”
维洛索后来进一步表示，苹果不仅采用了类似的产品理念，甚至连“Duo”这一名称都让他感到意外。他坦言，看到苹果最终也选择使用这一命名方式，令许多参与过该项目的人五味杂陈。
一些业内观察人士认为，微软在过去十余年中曾多次率先尝试新形态产品和创新理念，却未能转化为市场成功案例。从平板电脑、智能手机到双屏设备，微软往往率先提出概念，但最终由其他厂商将这些想法推向大众市场。
随着iPhone Duo获得广泛关注，关于Surface Duo是否“生不逢时”的讨论再次成为科技圈焦点。对于许多曾参与项目开发的人来说，苹果的成功未必意味着模仿，而更像是对微软当年探索方向的一次迟来验证。

units.text: Foldable displays tend to show a more visible crease over time, but Apple‘s Kate Bergeron says iPhone Duo has a replaceable cover layer on its folding screen to help mitigate that issue.
iPhone Duo ‘cover layer’ on folding display can be replaced over time for a day-one look

After the iPhone Duo was introduced last month, Apple execs gave interviews explaining how the company very intentionally sought to maximize durability and minimize crease issues that plague other foldables.
As part of that effort, it seems the iPhone Duo has a unique design feature to ensure a “day one” type experience for years to come: a replaceable cover layer on the folding display.
Here’s Kate Bergeron, Apple VP of Hardware Engineering, speaking to @angietutorials on TikTok:

“The matte display coating does a really nice job of, I’ll say minimizing the crease. But there’s a cover layer on top, and we’ve done a significant amount of engineering work to help that wear in as long of a manner as we can, and to make sure that you get the most out of that layer’s performance. It’s actually replaceable, which is a really nice thing for the customer, that you can peel off that layer and get a new one.”
You can watch the full clip here on TikTok.

Apple refers to this “cover layer” in its list of AppleCare estimated service costs for iPhone Duo. As spotted by Quinn Nelson, a cover layer replacement costs $19 with AppleCare. Its cost without coverage is currently unknown.
So if you’re worried about spending $2,000+ on an iPhone Duo only to find the display crease become more prominent over time, it sounds like Apple has a solution.

这一信息来自苹果硬件工程副总裁Kate Bergeron接受内容创作者Angelica Siciliani Fendi采访时的介绍。Bergeron表示，这层保护材料本身就是可更换的，用户可以将旧的覆盖层移除，然后安装新的覆盖层。苹果此前并没有在iPhone Duo发布时重点宣传这一设计，因此此次公开信息也引起了外界关注。
iPhone Duo采用苹果首款折叠式内屏，完全展开后形成一块连续的大尺寸显示区域。由于折叠屏最明显的问题之一就是屏幕中央的折痕，苹果在最外层加入了特殊的纳米纹理覆盖层，通过特殊表面处理降低反光，同时让屏幕中央的折叠区域不那么明显。
这层覆盖材料并不是普通的塑料保护膜。苹果此前公布的内屏结构显示，iPhone Duo的折叠屏由多达10层超薄材料组成，纳米纹理覆盖层采用苹果定制的聚合物材料，刚性比其他行业常见材料最高提高约40%。覆盖层表面还加入了抗划伤涂层，用于应对日常使用过程中的摩擦和轻微刮擦。
在覆盖层之下，苹果还加入了高强度玻璃结构以及位于最底部的钛金属板，用于提高整个柔性显示组件的强度。苹果还使用特殊胶黏材料，使不同层之间能够像书页一样相互滑动，从而在反复弯折过程中释放应力，降低显示屏受到的机械压力。
不过，即使采用这些设计，最外层纳米纹理覆盖层仍然属于长期直接面对用户操作和环境的部件。它可能随着时间推移出现划痕、磨损或者表面处理效果下降，而这些问题并不一定意味着OLED显示面板本身已经损坏。
因此，苹果将这一层设计成可以独立更换，对于折叠屏手机来说具有比较明显的实际意义。传统折叠屏设备如果内屏保护层出现严重磨损，维修往往可能涉及整个显示组件，而iPhone Duo理论上可以只更换最外层覆盖材料，从而避免因为保护层问题更换昂贵的整块折叠屏。
苹果已经公布了美国市场的相关维修价格。购买AppleCare+的iPhone Duo用户，如果需要更换这层覆盖材料，费用为19美元。苹果目前尚未公布没有AppleCare+情况下的官方更换价格。
目前也没有迹象表明苹果允许普通用户自行购买覆盖层并在家完成更换。虽然苹果高管使用了“可以剥离并更换”的描述，但实际维修流程仍很可能由Apple Store或苹果授权服务提供商完成。对于售价高达2999美元起的iPhone Duo来说，自行尝试拆卸内屏覆盖层并不是一个值得冒险的维修方案。
从维修角度来看，这一设计与普通智能手机的屏幕保护膜存在明显区别。普通保护膜主要承担防刮擦作用，用户可以自行撕掉并更换；而iPhone Duo的纳米纹理覆盖层同时属于折叠屏整体结构的一部分，其材料、表面纹理以及与下方显示组件之间的关系都经过专门设计，因此更换过程需要保持屏幕内部结构的完整性。
这一设计也与苹果此前对iPhone Duo折叠屏耐久性的强调有关。苹果表示，为了让内屏在长期反复折叠之后仍保持良好状态，公司进行了大量工程设计，并特别针对折痕、弯折应力以及表面耐久性进行了优化。
iPhone Duo的内屏并没有采用iPhone 18 Pro系列使用的Ceramic Shield 2，而是采用定制聚合物覆盖层。外屏则继续使用Ceramic Shield 2，背部同样采用Ceramic Shield。也就是说，iPhone Duo实际上根据两块屏幕所承担的不同任务，采用了完全不同的保护材料。
内外两块屏幕均支持ProMotion自适应刷新率、全天候显示和原彩显示，户外峰值亮度最高达到3000尼特。展开后的内屏是iPhone Duo最核心的使用体验，因此苹果需要在柔韧性、强度、抗划伤能力以及折痕控制之间进行平衡。
值得注意的是，能够更换外层覆盖材料并不意味着iPhone Duo的折痕可以永久消失。纳米纹理层主要作用是降低折痕的视觉存在感，如果OLED面板以及其内部结构经过长时间反复弯折后产生永久性形变，更换最外层覆盖材料并不能从根本上修复显示面板本身。
但对于日常使用而言，这仍然是一个具有实际意义的维修设计。折叠屏手机最大的长期使用风险之一就是内屏表面和折叠区域容易出现磨损，而iPhone Duo通过将最容易损耗的外层覆盖材料设计成独立可替换部件，可以把一部分维修从“更换整个屏幕”降低到“更换表面覆盖层”。
目前iPhone Duo将在10月16日开启预订，10月23日正式上市。随着首批用户开始长期使用，纳米纹理覆盖层究竟能够维持多久、实际更换需要多长时间，以及19美元的AppleCare+维修价格是否能够覆盖大多数相关情况，都将成为评价这套设计实际价值的重要因素。
从苹果目前公布的信息来看，iPhone Duo的可维修性并非体现在整机结构大幅模块化，而是通过将折叠屏中最容易发生长期磨损的外层组件独立出来，实现更加有针对性的维修。对于售价达到2999美元的首款折叠iPhone而言，这种设计也有助于降低用户在长期使用过程中面对高昂屏幕维修成本的风险。
